title: smime-tree error.rs: SmimeError::Other(String) and ::MalformedInput(String) use stringly-typed messages
description: SmimeError::Other(String) and SmimeError::MalformedInput(String) carry a free-form message string. Callers who want to distinguish sub-cases (e.g. 'CBC IV missing' vs 'no encrypted content') must parse the string. Stringly-typed error variants lose the values; structured variants keep them accessible. Idiomatic Rust: add sub-variants like MissingIv, NoEncryptedContent, AesCekWrongLength { got: usize, expected: usize }, etc. The Other variant can be retained for truly unclassifiable errors as a catch-all with #[non_exhaustive] already in place.
